categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build FAILS: CS0246 in Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/wwwroot/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml, a copy of the front page template the model left behind from a debugging experiment ('does the checker look under wwwroot/Views?'). The site therefore does not boot (check: site.boots FAIL), so / and both posts return nothing, and no screenshots could be taken (0+0+0). Even without the stray file, blocks would not render: every block grid value (front page and both posts) has expose entries with contentKey 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, which match no block. The model's own curl near the end confirmed the front page grid and post bodies rendered empty, and it stopped before fixing that. Images: 6 of the provided Unsplash photos imported via create-media filePath into a 'Blog Images' media folder, and views use GetCropUrl, but nothing is served (2/5). Domain '/' was deliberately put on the Blog page (plus a harmless wildcard *1103 entry) and all content is published, but the site does not answer (3/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: heroBlock, textBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are element types in Blocks/; blogFrontPage and blogPostPage are document types in Pages/ (8/8). One 'BlogBlockGrid' data type in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid with hero, rich text, image+caption and quote is used on both page types (7/7). siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPostPage, templates assigned (late, in a follow-up update), camelCase aliases (5/5). Post metadata (excerpt, heroImage, postDate) are real properties and there are no compositions. Deducted 2 in hygiene: post pages carry both a heroImage property, which the template renders as a header with the title, and a hero block with the same image and title, so each post shows its photo and title twice. blogFrontPage also has heading/introduction properties duplicating its own hero block.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both page templates use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); there is no custom loop and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are unchanged (7/7). The four adapters sit at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, take BlockGridItem<T>, map to a plain model and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup (6/6). There is one ViewComponent per block, rendering Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml, but the ViewComponent classes are in Models/Blocks/ next to the view models, in files named HeroBlock.cs etc., which echo the ModelsBuilder type names. TextModel also exposes Umbraco's IHtmlEncodedString, so it is not a fully plain model (5/7). Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations, friendly extensions and GetCropUrl are used, and Tailwind is built. Deducted for the litter left in the project: .tmp_beconv.cs, .tmp_bgconv.cs, .tmp_s.txt, .tmp_tree.json, .front.html and .post1.html in the solution root, the stray wwwroot/Views copy, and an inline <style> block for grid CSS in _Layout.cshtml (3/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two posts on topic: 'Why MCP Is Awesome' (~620 words, 6 blocks: hero, text, quote, text, image, text) and 'MCP: The Missing Link Between Agents and Your CMS' (~525 words, 5 blocks), with relevant circuit and network photos and credited captions. They are accurate but short and rather self-referential (4/6). Presentation can't be verified: the site doesn't build, there are no screenshots, and none of the block content rendered even during the run. The Razor and Tailwind code describes a coherent card listing and post layout (1/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: All schema, media and content went through the Umbraco MCP server (71 calls). Order of operations was followed: schema, then content, then stop, build and restart, then Razor. Stayed in the project folder with no memory access; the GitHub raw fetches of Umbraco source are allowed (3/3). The final report is not a report but an interim message: 'Now I'll re-save the value with expose entries and verify they persist:', after which the session ended. It mentions that the grids render empty but implies a fix that never happened, and says nothing about the stray wwwroot/Views file that breaks the build (0/2).

summary: Built a clean MCP schema (4 blocks in a shared block grid, front page and post types in the right folders) and textbook adapter/ViewComponent code. But it stopped mid-debugging: a stray wwwroot/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml breaks the build, and every block grid value's expose array has zero GUIDs, so no blocks would render anyway.
strengths: Correct document type folders and kinds; siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPostPage structure with real post metadata properties
Reusable block set (hero, rich text, image, quote) in one Custom/ block grid used on both page types
Rendering pipeline follows the convention exactly: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, alias-named adapters, one ViewComponent per block
Provided Unsplash photos imported over MCP into a media folder; '/' domain set deliberately

issues.text: dotnet build fails (CS0246) because of a leftover debugging copy at Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/wwwroot/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml; the site does not boot
Block grid values on Blog and both posts have expose entries with contentKey 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, so every grid renders empty (uSync/v18/Content/*.config)
The run ended on an interim message promising a fix that was never made; the final report doesn't disclose the broken state
Post pages render the heroImage header and a hero block with the same photo and title, so both appear twice (Views/blogPostPage.cshtml plus post content)
ViewComponent classes live in Models/Blocks/ in files named after the ModelsBuilder types (HeroBlock.cs etc.); TextModel exposes IHtmlEncodedString
Scratch files left in the solution root (.tmp_*.cs, .tmp_tree.json, .tmp_s.txt, .front.html, .post1.html)
